Table 2: Genotyping results for household patient pairs.
Figure 2: Genotype-matching proportions for all patient pairs. (a) Matching proportions and Clopper–Pearson exact 95% CIs are reported for each study and each genotyping method. Statistically robust studies with 95% CIs of <40% are represented with full opacity, while studies with 95% CIs of >40% are shown with transparency. Matching proportions from Crampin et al . and Glynn et al . are reported together under Malawi because these studies shared a patient cohort. (b) Proportions are shown as points scaled by study sample size, with the fitted generalized additive model curve and its 95% CI ribbon plotted against the TB incidence (patients per 100 000 person-years).
Figure 3: Genotype-matching proportions for secondary patient pairs. Matching proportions and Clopper–Pearson exact 95% CIs are shown for studies reporting matching for secondary household patient pairs. Co-prevalent household contact patients are excluded. Statistically robust studies are represented with full opacity, while studies with 95% CIs of >40% are shown with transparency. (b) Proportions are shown as points scaled by study sample size, with the fitted generalize curve and its 95% CI ribbon plotted against the TB incidence (cases per 100 000 person-years).
